candidates.change_summary: Replace the revert condition so that MinSum is always set, ignoring the initialized check.
Remove the lock check and state change from the nonReentrant modifier so that SetMinSum can be called even when locked.
Delete the revert statement inside the if block, allowing MinSum to be changed even after initialization.
Replace the conditional body with just setting MinSum unconditionally, removing the initialization guard.
Delete the require(!locked_) check, allowing reentrant calls that can bypass the guard in SetMinSum.
Delete the whole modifier body (keeping it empty), removing the non-reentrant protection completely so that SetMinSum can be called reentrantly.

Remove the nonReentrant_ modifier from SetLogFile so it can be called even when locked_ is true (reentrancy allowed), but the observable behavior change is that the function will no longer revert due to reentrancy guard, altering control flow and potentially allowing calls that previously reverted to succeed, which an external caller can detect via transaction success/failure and subsequent state reads.

Replace the require/revert condition in SetLogFile from if(intitalized)revert() to if(!intitalized)revert(), making the function revert when NOT initialized instead of when already initialized, completely inverting the initialization guard and changing when SetLogFile can be successfully called.
Delete the line `Log = LogFile(_log);` so that after SetLogFile completes, the Log state variable remains unchanged, meaning the intended update to Log never occurs.
Replace `Log = LogFile(_log);` with `Log = LogFile(address(0));` so that SetLogFile always sets Log to the zero address instead of the caller-provided address, changing the state variable value.

Delete the line `locked_ = true;` from the nonReentrant_ modifier, so the reentrancy lock is never engaged during function execution, allowing reentrant calls and altering the behavior of SetLogFile (and other functions) which can be externally observed via reentrancy attack success.

Delete the line `locked_ = false;` from the nonReentrant_ modifier, so the lock is never released after a call, permanently locking all nonReentrant_ functions including SetLogFile after a single successful call, which is observable by subsequent calls always reverting.
